newsitem.title: HUNGARY: CS First Boston downgrades Pannonplast to 'buy'.
newsitem.headline: CS First Boston downgrades Pannonplast to 'buy'.

text.p: CS First Boston downgraded Hungarian plastics group Pannonplast Rt's shares to "buy" from "strong buy" following the release of the company's result report for the January-September period.
"Our view on Pannonplast remains positive despite the downgrade in our earnings forecast," CS First Boston's Budapest-based analyst Spencer Jakab said in a company update.
"We have, however, downgraded our opinion from strong buy to buy since the stock has appreciated 25 percent since our 26 July report."
In its nine-month consolidated IAS figures released on Monday, Pannonplast reported net income of 1.064 billion forints for the period, 77.6 percent higher than in the same period of last year.
Its operating profit was up by 28.8 percent to 873 million forints while sales revenues rose by 10 percent to 6.848 billion forints.
"The results are somewhat weaker than what we had been expecting," Jakab said. "Gross margin deteriorated to 34.9 percent for Q1-3 after reaching over 40 percent during Q2." @
The deterioration indicates margins close to 30 percent for the third quarter, probably due to price discounts in the plastic pipe business, he added.

Pannonplast said in its results that while the average purchase price was lower than in the same period of last year, the price of finished products either did not change or fell in line with competitors.
Consequently, the company said, it did not raise prices in most product groups and in certain cases offered a discount.
Jakab said he did not anticipate further margin erosion during the fourth quarter.
"Gross margins for the full year should stabilise at just over 36 percent, roughly equivalent to their average level over Q1-3," he said.
CS First Boston remains optimistic about Pannonplast.
"Within the context of the market, Pannonplast (along with Zalakeramia) is one of the best organic growth companies available," Jakab said.
